title: No-Bake Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough Bars
summary: Cottage-cheese cookie dough with peanut butter, maple syrup, almond flour and dark chocolate chips, topped with melted chocolate and sea salt. No baking: freeze the base for 10 minutes, then refrigerate the chocolate-topped slab for 30 minutes. The source conflicts on vanilla quantity and bar yield; both are flagged below.
serves: 12 bars in the description; 5 bars in the spoken tutorial (unresolved)

ingredients.note: The tutorial gives ½ cup; Louis describes his amount as about 110 g. The description also gives ½ cup.

Unresolved source conflict: the automatic caption at 0:18 says '1 tsp of vanilla', while the public written recipe says '1 tbsp vanilla extract'. Neither is silently treated as a correction of the other.
The narration only says 'some'; the approximate weight comes from the public description.

steps.text: Put the cottage cheese, peanut butter, maple syrup and vanilla in a large bowl. Note the unresolved vanilla quantity conflict in the ingredient list.
Blitz the wet ingredients together with an immersion blender.
Add the almond flour and mix it into the blended ingredients.
Add the dark chocolate chips and mix again.
Line a separate glass container with baking parchment. Add the cookie dough and press it down evenly.
Freeze the pressed base for 10 minutes.

ingredients.note: The source does not state the block's weight or cocoa percentage.

ingredients.item: Butter, for melting with the chocolate
ingredients.note: The description says 'a little butter'; there is no measured quantity.

steps.text: Just before the base is ready, melt half a block of dark chocolate with a little butter, as specified in the written method. No melting temperature or time is supplied.
Pour the melted chocolate over the chilled cookie-dough base.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes. This is the stated method; Louis later admits that he accidentally used the freezer instead.
Cut into bars and sprinkle with sea salt. The description says 12 bars, while the spoken tutorial says 5; the source does not resolve the difference.

nutrition.note: Approximate creator-reported figures, not independently calculated or verified. The written method cuts 12 bars but the spoken tutorial says 5, so these figures must not be applied to a five-bar batch. Vanilla and chocolate-block size are also unresolved.

notes: Louis Howard's description credits @nora.dora99; the upload alternates tutorial narration with his recreation and commentary. The credited account has not been independently authenticated.

The first chill is explicitly 10 minutes in the freezer. The second is explicitly 30 minutes in the fridge. At 1:10 Louis says he accidentally used the freezer for the second chill and that the bars would have been easier to cut otherwise; that mistake is not substituted for the intended method.
The vanilla and yield conflicts are present in the source materials, not conversions or quantities invented for this entry. The recipe is marked partial because they remain unresolved.
The source does not establish a fat-loss benefit; Louis explicitly says it is not necessarily an answer to fat-loss goals. No such benefit is inferred from the nutrition label.
gaps: Vanilla quantity conflicts: 1 tsp in the spoken tutorial's automatic captions versus 1 tbsp in the written description.
Yield conflicts: 5 bars in the spoken tutorial versus 12 bars in the description.
No block weight or cocoa percentage for the dark chocolate, measured butter or salt quantity, or glass-container dimensions are supplied.
No storage duration, chilling temperature or melting method/time is specified. Nutrition is approximate and publisher-reported, not tested.

source.quantity_basis: Public video description plus 64 English automatic-caption segments. The description supplies the approximate 50 g chocolate chips, butter and nutrition; narration supplies wet ingredients, almond flour, half a block of chocolate and timing. Vanilla (1 tsp vs 1 tbsp) and yield (5 vs 12 bars) conflicts are preserved explicitly. Unmeasured butter and sea salt remain null.
